title: Econ telemetry demultiplexer and per-entity latency-cost fingerprinting
creator: Aisha Patel
description:
Problem: Current cost/latency rollups conflate multi-tenant traces and dynamic routing fallbacks (model variants, regional reroutes) which makes per-route/model/customer economics noisy and hard to explain. This ticket implements a telemetry 'demultiplexer' that separates interleaved spans and produces a stable per-entity latency and token-cost fingerprint suitable for Console dashboards and downstream billing ingestion.

Goals:
- Produce deterministic per-route, per-model, and per-customer cost/latency fingerprints for a rolling 30d window.
- Attribute shared GPU tokens and batching costs proportionally, using a heuristic that respects latency SLOs and causal span boundaries.
- Tag and persist variants: queued time, batching delay, KV cache hit/miss, model-quantization path, and fallback reason.
- Emit both high-cardinality raw events for debug and low-cardinality aggregate slices for the Console UI and billing pipelines.

Design notes / approach:
1) Ingest path: enrich runtime spans with routing metadata (route_id, model_variant, tenant_id, kernel_profile, seq_len_histogram). Where metadata is missing, use best-effort enrichment via request hashing and time-window alignment.
2) Demultiplexing algorithm: windowed stream processor that groups spans by causal root and a fingerprint key (tenant_id|route|model_variant|minute_bucket). We will use a two-pass approach: fast approximate grouping (HyperLogLog-ish sketch + bloom filter) to route to worker shards, followed by deterministic reconciliation that breaks ties using span parentage and request UUIDs.
3) Cost apportionment: compute three cost primitives per group: compute_cost (GPU time + kernel multiplier), memory_cost (KV cache impact), and infra_amortization (per-request orchestration costs). For shared batches, apportion by effective token shares adjusted by small SLO-preserving weights to avoid skewing latency-sensitive routes.
4) Fingerprinting: generate an opaque stable fingerprint per (route, model, tenant) that encodes recent median latency, p95, avg token-cost, and cache-hit-rate. Store fingerprint with TTL and version for time-series comparison.
5) Outputs: (a) raw demux events -> long-term debug store (GCS/Parquet), (b) aggregates -> OLAP table used by Console and billing rollup jobs, (c) drift alerts -> Redwood Optimize hooks when fingerprint deviates beyond thresholds.

Non-goals: This ticket does not change billing charges or legal invoicing; it only improves attribution signals. It also does not implement UI changes — Console tickets will follow once APIs are stable.

Success criteria:
- Aggregate attribution accuracy improvement: reduce cross-tenant leakage metric by >60% in a synthetic injection test.
- Fingerprints persisted for >=90% of high-volume routes over 30d.
- End-to-end processing latency for aggregates <= 5 minutes (nearline), with raw events available in 24 hours.

Open design trade-offs:
- Strict deterministic grouping vs eventual reconciliation: deterministic grouping gives explainability but is more expensive; we bias to reconciliation approach to keep cost bounded.
- Apportionment heuristics: conservative vs aggressive token-splitting. We selected SLO-preserving conservative weights to avoid penalizing latency-sensitive customers.

Artifacts and links:
- Design doc: https://redwood.atlassian.net/wiki/spaces/ENG/pages/ECON-DEMUX-2026 (internal)
- Prototype PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/telemetry/pull/789 (worker + streaming job)
- Synthetic test dashboard: https://grafana.redwood.ai/d/xyz/econ-demux-synthetic
- Downstream billing mapping spec: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/0B_example_mapping

Implementation plan (high level):
- Week 1: runtime span enrichment and sample ingestion; prototype sketching for fast grouping.
- Week 2: deterministic reconciliation job + simple apportioner; generate fingerprints and store in OLAP.
- Week 3: integrate drift alerting and Optimize hooks; run synthetic injections and measure leakage.
- Week 4: performance tuning, QA, rollback playbook, and handoff to Console & Billing teams for integration.
